A fossil record of extinction speaks to species' actual durations, which this modal and teleological wording does not assert.
rationale: The passage explains why there is generation, by a goal of species-level eternity. No measurement of births, deaths or extinctions distinguishes that goal from generation simply occurring. The claim is conceptual.

operationalization: Compare adult body-size distributions of vertebrates with invertebrates, and of motile animals with sessile ones, using medians and maxima. The claim holds if, taken generally, blooded animals are larger than bloodless ones and mobile animals larger than fixed ones.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: adult body mass for vertebrates

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: body length for a wide range of fishes, as the vertebrate aquatic sample

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: body size for marine invertebrates, including sessile and motile forms where length is recorded

obstacles: Aristotle's blood is approximately vertebrate blood, and some invertebrates exceed many vertebrates.
Colonial sessile animals have an ambiguous individual size.
Medians and maxima answer 'taken generally' in different ways, and invertebrate size coverage is biased toward large or commercial species.
rationale: Vertebrate body sizes are well tabulated, and marine invertebrate lengths are available for many species, so both contrasts can be sketched. Sessile and bloodless animals are the poorly standardized side, especially colonies. The result can support or weaken a general tendency and cannot yet match the full scope of animals.

operationalization: Measure egg diameter at laying and again during development for fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods, and for birds and oviparous reptiles. The claim holds if only the first three groups' eggs enlarge after they are produced.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: egg diameters and reproductive mode for fishes; the post-laying change itself is in embryological sources rather than the diameter field

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: egg and brood notes for crustaceans and cephalopods

obstacles: Teleost swelling is largely water uptake into the perivitelline space, which still counts as an increase in size.
Bird and reptile eggs are widely described as fixed in size after laying, while paired measurements are species-specific.
Brooded crustacean embryos are unevenly measured.
rationale: The contrast between cleidoic eggs and eggs that swell after laying is established for model fishes, poultry, a few reptiles and common cephalopods. Those published series can test the claim on a restricted set of species. There is no multi-group dataset of before-and-after diameters, so full taxonomic coverage remains out of a single analysis.

operationalization: Score live birth against the presence of vertebrate blood, and score vertebrates as viviparous, oviparous or sterile. The claim holds if every viviparous animal has blood and every animal with blood reproduces in one of those two ways unless it is infertile.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: live-bearing versus egg-laying in fishes, a major blooded group

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive notes for invertebrates, including viviparous arthropods where recorded

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: blood, hemolymph and reproductive mode for exemplar vertebrates and for viviparous invertebrates

obstacles: Aristotle's blood is red vertebrate blood, so viviparous insects and scorpions are the discriminating cases.
Live birth is coded for fishes and scattered for terrestrial invertebrates.
Sterile hybrids such as the mule have to be listed before the 'unless infertile' clause is applied.
rationale: Reproductive mode of vertebrates, especially fishes, is in open databases, and viviparity of several invertebrate groups is in species accounts. Joining those sources tests whether live birth occurs without vertebrate blood. Invertebrate coverage is the weak side, so the universal is partly, not fully, resolvable.
